Ideas.spark: Low-friction capture of sudden creative sparks or flash insights.
Ideas.concept-seed: Early-stage unrefined concepts needing further investigation.
Ideas.project-idea: Potential personal or technical project proposals awaiting evaluation.
Ideas.experiment: Specs or setups for personal trial-and-error experiments.

Reflections.introspection: First-person self-evaluations and personal state tracking.
Reflections.philosophical: Reflections on broad philosophical questions, ethics, or personal values.
Reflections.retrospective: Personal post-mortems on completed life phases or experiences.
Reflections.opinion: Subjective takes and evolving personal stances on non-objective topics.

Inquiries.open-question: Unresolved internal questions or curiosities needing exploration.
Inquiries.paradox: Contradictions or counter-intuitive concepts causing friction.
Inquiries.doubt: Expressed uncertainty regarding an existing mental model or assumption.

Mental Models.heuristic: Personal cognitive shortcuts or rules of thumb for decision-making.
Mental Models.framework: Internalized analytical lenses used to perceive and dissect systems.
Mental Models.principle: Core personal rules, tenets, and guiding operational philosophies.
Mental Models.lens: Alternative perspective frameworks applied to specific domains or contexts.

Medias.book: Books, e-books, and audiobooks consumed for learning or leisure.
Medias.show: TV series, mini-series, or serial shows.

Resources.article: Online blog posts, essays, news articles, or technical write-ups.
Resources.bookmark: Saved web links or quick reference pointers.
Resources.paper: Academic papers, research publications, or whitepapers.
Resources.tool: Software applications, developer tools, services, or utilities.
Resources.video: Reference video content, tutorials, or recorded talks.

Requirements.functional: User-facing behaviors, business rules, or functional capabilities.
Requirements.non-functional: Quality attributes such as performance, security, and scalability.
Requirements.business-rule: Domain constraints or business policies governing behavior.
Requirements.constraint: Hard technical, legal, or resource boundaries limiting design choices.

Specs.prd: Product Requirement Documents defining user goals and feature scope.
Specs.rfc: Request for Comments proposing technical changes or architecture.
Specs.feature-spec: Detailed technical specification for a specific feature implementation.
Specs.design-doc: Comprehensive design documents outlining system architecture, data models, and implementation plans.

Decisions.architecture: High-level structural choices, tech stack selections, or system boundaries.
Decisions.product: Strategic product decisions, trade-offs, and feature prioritization.
Decisions.process: Workflow, team organization, operational policy choices.

Standards.coding: Code style guides, linter rules, and programming conventions.
Standards.naming: Conventions for variables, files, APIs, and database schemas.
Standards.workflow: Standard procedures for git branches, deployments, and reviews.
Standards.operations: Incident handling, release checklists, and maintenance standards.

Architectures.database: Schemas, ER diagrams, data models, and storage engine designs.
Architectures.domain-model: Core business logic models, entities, and aggregates.
Architectures.service: Microservice descriptions, system boundaries, and service APIs.
Architectures.infrastructure: Cloud topology, hardware configurations, and network setups.
Architectures.api: REST/GraphQL contracts, endpoints, and interface specifications.
Architectures.data-flow: Pipelines, ETL processes, streaming architectures, and message flows.

Project Contexts.migration: Data, infrastructure, or code migration plans and progress tracking.
Project Contexts.legacy: Documentation of legacy components, technical context, and caveats.
Project Contexts.technical-debt: Tracked code smells, temporary workarounds, and cleanup needed.
Project Contexts.status: Periodic status updates, project health summaries, and milestone tracking.
Project Contexts.risk: Potential threats, failure modes, and mitigation strategies for a project.

Issues.bug: Unintended behaviors or defects in system execution.
Issues.task: Distinct, actionable work item to be completed.
Issues.improvement: Refactoring, optimization, or enhancement to existing capabilities.
Issues.incident: Production outages, severity alerts, or emergency interventions.
Issues.open-problem: Unresolved questions or technical roadblocks requiring investigation.
Issues.recurring: Recurring issues or patterns that need systematic handling.

Solutions.fix: Resolved solution applied to a bug or defect.
Solutions.workaround: Temporary fix or bypass for a known issue or limitation.
Solutions.troubleshooting: Diagnostic guides and root-cause analysis steps.
Solutions.recipe: Copy-paste code snippets, CLI commands, or operational scripts.

HowTos.guide: Step-by-step walkthrough for completing a process.
HowTos.cheatsheet: Quick-reference command lists, syntax guides, or shortcuts.
HowTos.runbook: Operational steps for system maintenance, deployments, or recovery.

Meetings.sync: Regular status alignments or standup notes.
Meetings.planning: Sprint, quarterly, or roadmap planning sessions.
Meetings.retrospective: Sprint or project post-mortems and action items.
Meetings.1on1: Discussion notes between manager and team member.

Roadmaps.curriculum: Master learning roadmap or broad study track overview.
Roadmaps.course: Structured class, book syllabus, or formal education track.
Roadmaps.module: Self-contained study unit, chapter, or milestone topic.

Core Knowledge.concept: Durable, project-agnostic mental models and theoretical definitions.
Core Knowledge.framework: Structured analytical models, system loops, or calculation methods.
Core Knowledge.principle: Universal heuristics, core rules, and fundamental design tenets.
Core Knowledge.culture: General-culture knowledge, nice to know but outside the main thread (from a film, a trip, a talk).

Syntheses.case-study: Real-world examples, business case breakdowns, or practical applications.
Syntheses.research: In-depth evaluations, comparative studies, or literature reviews.
Syntheses.reference-anchor: Pointers to external source material, datasets, or benchmark figures.

Emergent Thoughts.open-question: Unresolved doubts, technical confusion, or points requiring further study.
Emergent Thoughts.idea: Actionable original insights, trading strategies, or design concepts.
Emergent Thoughts.hypothesis: Testable conjectures or speculative working theories.

Annotations.question: Questions or curiosities that arise while reading or studying.
Annotations.evidence: Supporting facts, stats, or references cited in the source.
Annotations.conclusion: Summaries, takeaways, or final thoughts on a topic.
Annotations.extract: Bigger ideas or concepts extracted from the source.

Assets.code: Production-grade code snippets or repository references.
Assets.script: Automation scripts, shell tools, or quick utilities.
Assets.diagram: Visual architectural diagrams, flowcharts, or system maps.
Assets.dataset: Test datasets, CSVs, or sample data payloads.
Assets.mockup: UI/UX designs, wireframes, or prototype links.
Assets.document: Formal documents, reports, or structured write-ups.

Journals.daily: Daily log entry capturing tasks, notes, and log items.
Journals.weekly: Weekly recap, accomplishments, and focus areas.
Journals.reflection: Periodic introspection on personal or professional progress.
Journals.scratchpad: Disposable scratch notes, temporary calculations, or working space.
Journals.project-log: Chronological activity log specific to a project.

Indexes.global-index: Master directory or root entry point of the vault.
Indexes.topic-index: Curated index page for a specific knowledge domain.

MoCs.domain-moc: Map of content connecting all notes in a specific domain.
MoCs.project-moc: Central navigation hub for a specific project.
MoCs.area-moc: Map of content tracking an area of responsibility.
